feed.title: NPR Topics: World
feed.subtitle: NPR world news, international art and culture, world business and financial markets, world economy, and global trends in health, science and technology. Subscribe to the World Story of the Day podcast and RSS feed.

entry.title: The United Nations General Assembly is meeting. Is it accomplishing anything?
entry.summary: NPR's Mary Louise Kelly speaks with Michael Froman, Council on Foreign Relations president, at the UN General Assembly.

entry.title: Sri Lanka court convicts 15 over deadly 2019 Easter bombings
entry.summary: The Islamic State group-inspired attacks were among the deadliest in Sri Lanka's history, killing 42 foreigners.

entry.title: CNN, MS NOW and Politico sue Trump. And, Paramount settles in massive merger lawsuit
entry.summary: CNN, MS NOW and Politico have sued Trump after the networks were suspended from the White House. And, Paramount makes concessions to resolve a lawsuit over its massive Warner Bros. Discovery merger.

entry.title: Houthis try to push deeper into western Yemen, upending life, witnesses tell NPR
entry.summary: As the U.S. conflict with Iran drags, the Iranian-backed Houthis in Yemen have opened a new front, taking new territory and displacing more than 100,000 people.

entry.title: A journalist once barred from the White House says this media ban is different
entry.summary: Jim Acosta has already been through a White House press-pass fight. Now, three news organizations are barred, and he says the press is showing solidarity that should have come sooner.

entry.title: Trump heads to the U.N. looking for wins after a rough week
entry.summary: The past couple of weeks have been particularly challenging for Trump with a series of legal and political setbacks.

entry.title: War between U.S. and Iran becomes a test of who will blink first
entry.summary: More than six months into the conflict between the U.S. and Iran, it's become a high-stakes game of endurance.

entry.title: Leaders set ambitious goals to better the world by 2030. They've made little progress
entry.summary: In 2015, global leaders set ambitious goals to reduce inequality, end hunger and boost education. More than a decade later, the world is nowhere near achieving much of what was promised.

entry.title: Political scientist on what's at stake as Trump speaks to world leaders at UNGA
entry.summary: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with political scientist Ian Bremmer of the Eurasia Group about President Trump's diplomatic stakes as he addresses the U.N. General Assembly.

entry.title: A new book by Princess Diana's brother prompts war of words with King Charles III
entry.summary: A new book by the late Princess Diana's brother, Charles Spencer, has made headlines with damning allegations about King Charles III. Buckingham Palace responded with a strongly-worded statement.
